Dar al-Masnavi's Song of the Reed page sets twenty-odd renderings side by side under numbered headings, and heading 4, Translation by Nicholson, 1926, gives line 1 as: Listen to this reed how it complains: it is telling a tale of separations. Word for word as shipped, colon and all, and ending in a full stop on that page, so the terminal stop is not even editorial. It is distinguished on the same page from heading 5, Rhymed (Abbreviated) Translation by Nicholson, 1950, which is the different, versified Nicholson people confuse it with, and from Whinfield 1887, Arberry 1961, Barks 1994 and the rest. The date is right too: Nicholson's Gibb Memorial translation of Books I and II is the 1926 volume. Locator: line 1 of Book I, the opening line of the Masnavi, correct. Attribution: Rumi's, and not on the misattribution list; the Dance, when you are broken open line in the brief's own CFL candidate list is the Barks trap, and this is not it. Scope: thirteenth century, a named poem by a named poet, and not scripture: the Masnavi is a didactic poem, not liturgy, so the Library rule does not reach it. Publishable. First, the tag is Poetry while the quotation runs as prose with no slashes: that is correct here, because rule 7 asks for the lineation of the edition named and Nicholson 1926 is a prose translation printed as numbered prose lines; the *** that Dar al-Masnavi inserts is that site's own hemistich marker, applied to every rendering on the page including the verse ones, and it is not Nicholson's lineation. Second, the source line calls the work The Masnavi while the named edition is titled The Mathnawi of Jalalu'ddin Rumi. That is a transliteration of the same title and the common English reading form, so it is not a wrong citation and I have not proposed a swap, but an editor who wants the source to echo the edition exactly could set The Mathnawi and stay at 91 characters.
